He was a four-year starter for the [[Oregon Ducks|Ducks]], and finished his career with 13.1 points, 3.5 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game. ==High School== A high profile recruit out of [[Franklin High School (Washington) | Franklin High]] in Seattle, Brooks "earned just about every honor possible" and led his team to the Washington 4A state championship as a senior [http://www.goducks.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=4295&SPID=235&DB_OEM_ID=500&ATCLID=22260&Q_SEASON=2006]. Aaron Jamal Brooks (known affectionately as “AB”) was born on January 14, 1985, in Seattle, Wash. His parents are Alvertis Brooks, Sr., and Bernardean Hampton. Aaron has one older brother, Alvertis, Jr., who played basketball at [[Seattle University]]. ==College== In his first year at Oregon, Brooks took over the starting point guard role previously occupied by current [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] guard [[Luke Ridnour]]. Despite missing 10 games with a broken bone in his wrist, Brooks earned Pac-10 All-Freshman honors. Brooks was named honorable mention all-Pac-10 for his efforts as a sophomore, a season which included a 34 point effort against [[USC Trojans basketball|USC]]. After a disappointing junior year at Oregon culminating in a suspension during a game against Washington, Brooks rebounded to become one of the leading candidates for Pac-10 Player of the Year. He led the Ducks to a number of key victories, including game winners over then #1 ranked [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and then #10 [[Arizona Wildcats basketball|Arizona]] [[McKale Center|in Tucson]]. Brooks scored a team high 31 points and grabbed 8 rebounds in an overtime road win against then top 25 ranked Washington State, helping to hand the Cougars their first home loss of the 2006-07 season. At the half-way mark of [[Pac-10]] conference play, Brooks was averaging 19.1 points and 4.5 assists per game in leading Oregon to a top 10 ranking and a 19-2 overall record. The Ducks went on to finish in a tie for third place in the Pac-10, and won the Pac-10 Championship tournament following an impressive three day romp over Arizona, Cal and USC. Oregon advanced to the Midwest Regional Final where they lost to defending champion [[Florida Gators basketball|Florida]]. On March 5th, Brooks was announced as one of 22 finalists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]], which is given to the top college basketball player in the nation. On March 28th, Brooks was one of 10 players named to the Wooden All-American Team. He won the men's three point shootout on March 29, 2007, to finish off his NCAA career.[http://www.freep.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070330/SPORTS06/703300474]. His major is political science. == NBA == At the NBA's 2007 pre-draft camp, Brooks was the lightest player measured, at 161 pounds.
